title: The Verge’s guide to the best gifts under $100
snippet: Even in an era of inflation like the one we're living through now, $100 can still buy a lot… if you know where to look. In fact, it's enough to get something useful and well-made, but not so pricey that it's likely to leave you with lingering guilt or lead to insurmountable debt. As reviewers, shoppers, and endless tinkerers ourselves, we're well-versed in recommending stuff in this price tier. Below, you'll find our favorite items at $100 or less that we think are fun, eccentric, and surprisingly handy. From open-style earbuds and gaming gear to handheld vacuums and e-readers, our picks should suit just about anyone on your sho … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Even in an era of inflation like the one we’re living through now, $100 can still buy a lot… if you know where to look. In fact, it’s enough to get something useful and well-made, but not so pricey that it’s likely to leave you with lingering guilt or lead to insurmountable debt.

As reviewers, shoppers, and endless tinkerers ourselves, we’re well-versed in recommending stuff in this price tier. Below, you’ll find our favorite items at $100 or less that we think are fun, eccentric, and surprisingly handy. From open-style earbuds and gaming gear to handheld vacuums and e-readers, our picks should suit just about anyone on your shopping list, at a price most can get behind.

How much do you want to spend?

$75

Camp Snap’s 110D is like catnip for vintage camera nerds. The digital point-and-shoot offers basic 8-megapixel resolution, a built-in flash, and filter compatibility, letting you capture both wide-angle and macro shots. Its photos likely won’t win you any awards, but its stylish, tactile design makes it a blast to give and get as a gift.

$52

If you’re contemplating a pricey pair of sleep buds for your loved one, we urge you to halt and consider a softer (and cheaper) alternative. Piercing pillows, designed with pockets for freshly pierced ears, also work great for regular earbuds. Blissbury’s comfy and adjustable Ear Pillow is our favorite. Problem — and sleep issues — solved.

$60

We’re big fans of Epilogue’s Operator Series, which lets you play retro game cartridges on a macOS or Windows machine with streamlined emulator software. Like the company’s Game Boy Operator, the Super Nintendo / Famicom version offers a simple way to play, save, and copy those old cartridges over a USB-C connection.

$60

Built for jet setters, Anker’s 100W travel adapter features a durable design, a handy LCD display to track charge percentage, and compatibility in over 200 countries. It doesn’t support AC plugs, but it does have four USB inputs for all your portables, including a trio of USB-C ports.

$55

Portable electronics seem to be all about going foldable these days, and why shouldn’t keyboards get in on the fun? Keychron’s B11 Pro is a swell gift for anyone who likes to pack an on-the-go keyboard, with concave keys, an ergonomic layout, and versatile connectivity over Bluetooth, USB-C, or 2.4GHz.

$60

Anker’s 140W hub is a stellar gift for anyone short on plugs but loaded with gadgets. It turns a single AC outlet into two and provides four USB ports in total. That means you can charge two USB-C gadgets and two USB-A devices at once while still powering more demanding products.

$10

No, it’s not a AAA membership for 24-hour roadside service — your giftee’s parents probably already bought them that. An A24 membership is much more fun, since it includes movie tickets to every weird, wild, and existential A24 film that hits theaters, plus zines, merch perks, and more.

$71

BougeRV’s fancy, compact lamp will spark joy for the glamper in your life, as well as everyone else. Its powerful, foldable spread of LEDs provides a blast of light anywhere plug-ins can’t reach, from the beach to the shed where that scary spider holds court, with up to 60 hours of light on low power.

$84

If a Kindle won’t quite fit into your favorite traveler’s tight pack job, consider the Xteink X4 Pro. The tiny e-reader is easy to pop into your bag or pocket thanks to its 4.3-inch display, and the latest model offers a backlit touchscreen for a more intuitive way to explore the literary world.

$59

Open-style earbuds can compromise bass quality, but the convenience of an airy, clip-on option that keeps your ear canals open is hard to overstate. CMF’s Clip Pro leverage the Nothing offshoot’s talents for slick design in an affordable package, offering solid performance, fun features, and serious comfort.

$47

For the phone-addicted person in your life, there’s Brick. The physical key lets users block up to 50 time-dissolving apps, from X to TikTok, while still letting them access essential software. It’s too bad that some of us need tech like this, but perhaps using it for a while will help you find the balance you need.

$55

The first 3D Zelda game has been remade for the modern era. And if you fear it will diverge too much from the Nintendo 64 original, fear not: This carefully crafted remake delivers updated graphics and improved controls alongside the same stellar adventure we remember.

$39

It seems melodramatic to say a good power drill can change your life, but anyone who does a lot of DIY projects knows it’s at least partially true. The Power Driver from Skil offers simplified driving, drilling, and screwdriving with up to 200 inch-pounds of torque and USB-C charging to tackle a range of jobs.

$79

Google’s orb-shaped Home Speaker is impressive in terms of design and sound quality, especially for a speaker this compact. We’re less enthused about Gemini’s sluggish response time, but it offers intuitive conversational understanding, and the speaker’s ability to link with Matter and Thread devices adds real convenience.

$99

For giftees with pets and / or children, there’s no such thing as having too many vacuums on hand. The cordless Ryobi One Plus perfectly bridges the gap between a robovac and stand-up models. With powerful suction and handy accessories, it’s just the ticket for quick cleanups, especially in the car, on stairs, and in between couch cushions.

$64

We all do it: pay a ton for a monthly streaming service for just a few series. It’s better to own the real thing, and Hacks, a hilarious drama that follows a comedian (Jean Smart) and her young writer (Hannah Einbinder) in the tumultuous “biz,” is one of HBO’s best series in years.

$70

The Switch 2 is a great device for gaming on the go, but its bulky dock is tough to pack. Genki’s pocket-sized brick is a brilliant alternative, with USB-C, USB-A, and HDMI 2.1 passthrough for displaying Switch 2 (and other handheld) games on your TV without Nintendo’s first-party behemoth.

$100

Hoto’s soldering iron is super cool — and by that we mean hot, as it’s able to reach nearly 400 degrees Fahrenheit in about three seconds. The cordless, adjustable iron makes the perfect gift for your favorite DIYer, especially since it features customizable presets for virtually any job.

$66

If you’re looking to spice up your barbecue or tailgate party, look no further than Igloo’s KoolTunes. The retro-inspired boombox cooler holds up to 26 cans and, for a twist, features a built-in Bluetooth speaker with up to 10 hours of battery life.

$79

You can give the gift of lost-then-found with a four-pack of Apple’s AirTags. With seamless, accurate tracking, they’re the perfect way for iPhone owners to locate everything from luggage to puppies. The latest models also have better tracking and louder sirens, boosting your chances of reuniting with your favorite things.

$45

Cold brew is as expensive as it is delicious, but it doesn’t have to cost you a ton. Oxo’s excellent Cold Brew Coffee Maker provides a way around the cold brew tax, without the hassle. Its overnight brew method provides storable, low-acid results so your favorite giftee can get their chill fill straight from the fridge instead of the cafe.

$100

Mobile gaming is a big business, but not everyone likes playing on a touchscreen. Accessories like the Prio make it easier, and unlike competing options, Razer’s solution gets super small. The controller folds down to fit in your pocket and expands to seven inches for full-sized control and compatibility with a bunch of modern phones.

$56

If you have a budding filmmaker in your circle, give them this tunable smart light and watch them work. Unlike most color bulbs, the Accent B7c has a built-in battery that lets it run for up to 70 minutes when unscrewed, and it offers granular, flicker-free control for perfect scene lighting.

$84

Reto’s Kodak-branded camera offers some neat tricks for $99. It uses 35mm film and glass elements in the lens, while adding modern extras like auto-wind, rewind, and an automatic flash. Its coolest features include a double-exposure setting that lets artistic shooters create stylish photos on glorious film, plus two focus points.

$84

Packing light is essential for all travelers, but it’s particularly vital for those who trek long distances. This high-capacity Nitecore charger is a killer addition to any pack, with water resistance, fast charging, and a slim, lightweight design that can power your devices without weighing them down.

$63

Pokopia brings Pokémon to life in a cozy worldbuilding game that borrows the best from predecessors like Minecraft and Animal Crossing. The twist? The slow-burning Switch 2 title eventually rolls into an expansive adventure that lets you customize as you go.

$60

For those who enjoy clever devices that just work, we give you Nimble’s “breakable” SharePower Portable Charger. The magnetically joined power bank quickly snaps into a pair of 20W batteries, letting two people charge their phones, or works as a single 10,000mAh unit for larger top-offs.

$48

For those tired of experiencing Joy-Con drift with their Nintendo Switch (or stick drift on any controller), there’s the TT Pro. Loaded with the latest anti-drift tech for joysticks and customizable triggers that let picky gamers have it their way, GuliKit’s customizable wireless controllers work with PlayStation, Nintendo, PC, iOS, and Android devices.

Update, November 25th: Updated to include new retail links and reflect current pricing.

fullText:
Walmart appears to have dropped support for Apple Pay on its website and in its iPhone app. This comes just a few weeks after the retailer finally added support for Apple’s payment platform to its app and website. 

9to5Mac is supported by Sony: Score Sony’s ULT Field 1 Bluetooth speaker for 51% off. Powerful bass, room-filling sound, up to 12 hours of battery life, IP67 durability, stereo pairing support, and much more.

Appleosophy spotted the change last week. There’s no indication whether the feature was removed deliberately or if this is some sort of bug. 

David Becker explains: 

In the “Payment method” section of the checkout page on Walmart’s app and website, it no longer lists Apple Pay as an accepted payment method where it previously did. Not only that, but it doesn’t show up under the “Other ways to pay” or “More ways to pay” sections of the checkout page either.

Walmart still accepts Apple Pay in its retail stores. The retailer began rolling out contactless payment support in August, including Apple Pay, Google Pay, contactless cards, and more. For years, Walmart refused to support Apple Pay, instead trying (and failing) to convince shoppers to use its own Walmart Pay platform. 

We’ll update this post if Walmart comments on Apple Pay’s disappearance from its website and app. Hopefully, it’s a bug that the company fixes sooner rather than later.

fullText:
Apple’s iPad lineup is incredibly strong, and two standout options are the iPad Air and iPad Pro. If you’re trying to decide whether the iPad Pro is worth the extra cost this holiday season, here’s everything you need to know.

11-inch M5 iPad Pro: Up to $300 off

Bonus pick: The all-new iPad mini is up to $100 off for Black Friday as well. 

iPad Air

Apple updated the iPad Air earlier this year, bringing the M4 chip for improved performance along with 12GB of RAM, up from 8GB in the previous generation.

The iPad Air is available in 11-inch and 13-inch screen sizes, and uses an LCD display with a 60Hz refresh rate. This means it doesn’t offer OLED or ProMotion, unlike the iPad Pro. It uses Touch ID for biometric authentication, supports the Magic Keyboard and Apple Pencil Pro, and offers the full iPadOS multitasking experience.

The iPad Air is available in four colors: blue, purple, starlight, and space gray. It starts at 128GB of storage and can be configured up to 1TB.

13-inch M4 iPad Air 1TB $1,449 (Reg. $1,549)

iPad Pro

The iPad Pro is the best iPad money can buy. It’s powered by Apple’s M5 chip and offers many advantages over the iPad Air.

The biggest difference is the display technology. The iPad Pro is available in 11-inch and 13-inch sizes and uses Apple’s Ultra Retina XDR display with tandem OLED technology. This means it offers deeper blacks, better contrast, and higher brightness than the LCD screen found in the iPad Air.

The iPad Pro also supports ProMotion with adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz. This means scrolling, animations, Apple Pencil interactions, and more will be significantly smoother.

Contrary to what the naming implies, the iPad Pro is also noticeably thinner and lighter than the iPad Air. The 11-inch iPad Pro measures 5.3mm thick, while the 13-inch model is even thinner at 5.1mm.

The iPad Pro offers Face ID instead of Touch ID, Thunderbolt connectivity, a four-speaker audio system, and nano-texture display options with the higher-end configuration.

9to5Mac’s Take

For most people, the iPad Air is the right choice. It delivers the entire iPad experience, excellent performance, and comes in four fun colors and two different screen sizes.

The iPad Pro is the best iPad you can buy, but it’s overkill for most people. Don’t get me wrong, I love my iPad Pro. If it’s in your holiday budget, it’s a fantastic choice. I can’t overstate how impressive the tandem OLED display is. It’s significantly better than the LCD screen on the iPad Air. It’s also great having Face ID in the iPad form factor.

The iPad Pro is slightly more tempting at its current sale price, with the mid-range 13-inch model at an impressive $350 off.

Still, both the iPad Air and iPad Pro run the same iPadOS experience, and that’s why I think the iPad Air is the better value for most people. What do you think? Let us know down in the comments.

title: TIME’s Top 100 Photos of 2026 list includes a shot taken on iPhone 18 Pro
snippet: In September, Apple held a photography exhibition in New York City to show off the iPhone 18 Pro camera. Now, an image of the Bugaboo Mountains from that exhibit, shot by photographer Jimmy Chin, is included in TIME’s Top 100 Photos. more…
fullText:
In September, Apple held a photography exhibition in New York City to show off the iPhone 18 Pro camera. Now, an image of the Bugaboo Mountains from that exhibit, shot by photographer Jimmy Chin, is included in TIME’s Top 100 Photos.

TIME publishes its Top 100 Photos list each year. The list showcases the pictures that the TIME Photo Department determines best capture that particular year.

The essence of TIME’s Photos of the Year, selected by our photo editors and presented below, is the authentic, sometimes staggering, reality captured by photojournalism. Someone was there. A news photographer lifted a viewfinder, pressed a button, and captured an instant happening in front of them.

Chin’s image was shot in Bugaboo Provincial Park, Canada, on iPhone 18 Pro. He explained that a traditional production creates a layer of separation between the photographer and the subject, with equipment, crew, and all the moving parts of a shoot. Shooting on iPhone 18 Pro meant that he could create a more intimate environment, allowing for a sense of comfort and spontaneity that comes through in the images.

Image Courtesy of Apple (as featured in the What Holds Us exhibition)

Chin’s goal was to capture the intersection of human ambition and the pursuit of wonder against the backdrop of a timeless natural landscape.

Here’s Chin:

“The resolution and the sharpness on iPhone 18 Pro surprised me. I could shoot a few inches of rock and ice, or a massive panorama, and trust it would hold at size. That is what this work needed. It also meant I carried almost nothing. In the mountains, everything you carry is a decision. I was not thinking about gear. I was thinking about what was in front of me.”

Apple’s “What Holds Us” exhibit ran in New York City in September, featuring work from photographers Alex Prager, Jack Davison, and Jimmy Chin, with each artist using the iPhone 18 Pro to explore the “people, places, and ideas that connect and ground humanity.” Kathy Ryan, the former longtime director of photography for The New York Times Magazine, curated the exhibition.

The exhibit is now headed to London, where it will open to the public on December 4, from 10 a.m. to 8 p.m. It will also be open from Saturday, December 12 through Sunday, December 13, from 10 a.m. to 6 p.m.

title: Galaxy Z Fold 8 features: What you can do on a foldable
snippet: Folding phones have come in numerous variations over the years as the concept has evolved. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the latest evolution that introduces a form factor that fits every user. Its unique design makes it a foldable most people can actually use – which makes it a perfect gift. You might be surprised by what it can do. more…
fullText:
Folding phones have come in numerous variations over the years as the concept has evolved. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is the latest evolution that introduces a form factor that fits every user. Its unique design makes it a foldable most people can actually use – which makes it a perfect gift. You might be surprised by what it can do.

This post is sponsored by Samsung.

Unfold for a bigger canvas

It’s in the name. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 folds and unfolds like other foldable devices – that much you know. But what the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s form factor provides is something different to what most might be familiar with.

Instead of a tall device that unfolds into a near-uniform square display, you get a wider screen more like a tablet. That makes it perfect for watching videos or movies. Content that naturally works well on TVs or your computer will look great on the Galaxy Z Fold 8.

	

What about content that’s best viewed in portrait mode? Because it opens up to a tablet-like display, you can turn the Fold 8 to watch YouTube Shorts or Instagram Reels without a problem, so if you or someone you know likes to watch content on a bigger display, the Z Fold 8 makes that much easier. It really doesn’t matter what content you come across – the wider inner display gives you that large screen feeling.

Fold for a minimal display

Like a well-designed tool, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 has more purposes than the tasks best suited for the inner display. That shorter, wider profile makes the outer display smaller, but not as thin as something on other foldables, like the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra.

In reality, the aspect ratio is similar enough across both the inner and outer screens that most content scales well on the shorter front panel. Social apps like X and Instagram look great because videos and images are able to fill the screen, rather than squeeze. Samsung’s One UI software also supports app optimization across both screens, although the experience may vary by app.

Saying the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s outer display is “minimal” isn’t a dig, either. Apps can be refreshing to use when you don’t need to open them on a large scale. Take Messages, for instance. It’s not a complex app, and there isn’t a ton to see – just the last couple of messages exchanged. The same goes for plenty of apps available on the Google Play Store.

And guess what? If you don’t like using the app on a smaller display, just unfold the phone. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is such a versatile phone, whether it’s a gift during the holidays or one for yourself.

Run three apps (or more) at once

There are instances where you need the large real estate. One UI 9 gives the Galaxy Z Fold 8 the option to open and run multiple apps on your screen. There are several ways you can do it, too.

The main approach is to split two apps on the wide inner display. But if you want to see more from one app, you can simply drag the split over in one direction. One UI 9 leaves room to add one more app to that split screen, giving you a three-way Split View. All it takes is dragging an app from the taskbar and choosing the spot.

If you truly need a fourth app open, you have the option to open another in a floating window. Having four apps open at once is definitely a niche instance, but the Galaxy Z Fold 8 handles it like it’s nothing. You can have YouTube up in one corner while you check Messages for gift ideas and shop through the Amazon app. It might be helpful to keep a list of what you got and for whom in a floating Sheets window.

The point is not only that it’s technically possible, but it’s usable. So often devices let users open apps in split screen, but are in no way comfortable enough for the task. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is perfect for it, and the experience actually makes you more productive, not less.

Built-in tripod

Most phones don’t let you get the best angle without any sort of third-party accessory. The Galaxy Z Fold 8, though, acts like its own tripod in a way.

Let’s say you’re taking photos, and you need to get a shot of yourself, but no one is around to take the photo for you. The Galaxy Z Fold 8’s hinge lets it prop itself up, so you can do things like set a timer and run to strike a pose.

This comes in handy for videos, too. Think of how many times you wanted to get a good angle on a plane or somewhere where there’s this flat surface just asking for a tiny tripod or kickstand. Well, the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is its own kickstand and can be positioned at just the right angle.

Where to buy the Galaxy Z Fold 8

fullText:
The industry’s biggest players are joining together to celebrate all the amazing VR games you probably don’t know about (but should).

This year has been difficult for the gaming industry at large, and that’s particularly true for the wonderful niche of VR gaming. Despite some huge setbacks, VR gaming is still alive and well, popping out tons of amazing games this year that you may not have realized. The full list of winners and nominees will be announced during the show, but Creature highlights Forefront, Thief VR: Legacy of Shadow, Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Empire City, Dungeons of Eternity, Titan Isles, and the ever-popular Hot Dogs, Horseshoes & Hand Grenades 2 as some of the most notable. title: Clicks Communicator hits a supply chain snag, and it isn’t because of RAM
snippet: Clicks is still on track to release the phone with a physical keyboard within the next few months, but a Communicator launch before the end of this year isn’t looking very likely as shipping gets pushed back. more…
fullText:
Clicks is still on track to release the phone with a physical keyboard within the next few months, but a Communicator launch before the end of this year isn’t looking very likely as shipping gets pushed back.

The Communicator is a fresh take on what an Android phone can be. It was first introduced at CES earlier this year, with the main selling angle being the physically integrated keyboard. Clicks wants to target those who are looking for a second device, and the Communicator fits the bill.

Last we heard, the Clicks Communicator was on track to launch and ship in December, following a cheery update detailing an upgrade to 12GB of RAM and other changes. However, Clicks posted a new update today stating that the timeline has shifted out a month because of supply chain issues caused by something other than RAM.

Unfortunately, we’ve encountered a delay with securing a critical supply chain component needed to fabricate our printed circuit board ahead of manufacturing and final assembly. Assembly will now begin in early January, with deliveries expected to start in late January.

It notes that the “critical supply chain component” is the essential fabric used for the company’s printed circuit boards. The blog post dives into some neat details about the component holding things up. The PCBs Clicks is using are made up of more material layers than some competitor boards. But the fabric used to layer those boards is in short supply at this sort of demand, with four manufacturers reportedly unable to meet the company’s required volume.

	

The post also spells out difficulties caused by troubles in the Middle East, and rising memory costs straining the chain of supply further, even if memory – surprisingly – isn’t the cause of this small delay. Those compounded issues have pushed production back, and users are now told to expect their Clicks Communicator pre-orders to be shipped in late January, at the earliest. Many pre-orders will likely be shipped after that because of further time constraints before Chinese New Year.

In an act of good faith, Clicks says it’s including a set of 3.5mm wired headphones in each box for orders placed prior to today.

A push from December to January isn’t massive, and Clicks still seems to be making solid time on developing a form factor we don’t often see. You can still pre-order the Clicks Communicator starting at $649.

iOS 27 includes a really clever new feature that aims to solve the awkward middle ground between cellular and Wi-Fi connectivity. Here’s how it works and how you can turn it on.

In a support document, Apple explains that Connectivity Assist uses cellular data to improve your connection when Wi-Fi is slow or unusable. Apple uses examples like your backyard or driveway, as well as “coffee shops, airports, sports venues, and everywhere in between.”

Essentially, the feature detects when your Wi-Fi connection is weak or unusable and intelligently uses cellular data to keep you connected.

One practical example I’ve noticed is when I walk out of my house and get in my car. Oftentimes, my iPhone will cling to my house’s weak Wi-Fi connection, making it hard to start playing Apple Music and queue up directions in Apple Maps.

Connectivity Assist solves that problem. My phone can now intelligently use cellular data to help that transition away from Wi-Fi. It’s one of many really nice quality-of-life improvements in iOS 27.

You can turn Connectivity Assist on or off with these steps:

Open the Settings app

Tap Wi-Fi

Scroll down and toggle Connectivity Assist on or off

Here are a couple of tidbits from Apple:

If you want to always stay on Wi-Fi for a specific router configuration, you can turn off Connectivity Assist for that particular network.

Connectivity Assist isn’t used when your iPhone is international roaming, in cellular Low Data Mode, or with some third-party apps that stream audio and video.

Another thing to be aware of is that you might use more cellular data with Connectivity Assist turned on. You can monitor your data usage via your carrier’s app or website, as well as in the Settings app on iPhone.

title: Samsung might copy the iPhone’s Dynamic Island soon, but it actually looks good [Video]
snippet: A new leak suggests that Samsung is preparing to copy the iPhone’s Dynamic Island feature in the not-too-distant future, to an extent that not many other Android brands have even done thus far. more…
fullText:
A new leak suggests that Samsung is preparing to copy the iPhone’s Dynamic Island feature in the not-too-distant future, to an extent that not many other Android brands have even done thus far.

Copying the Dynamic Island was briefly like a rite of passage for some Android brands, with many wasting almost no time in delivering their own version of the feature. But, on many of those devices, it’s a surface-level ripoff at best. The feature is primarily limited to music apps and timers, rarely working with any third-party apps in meaningful ways. Android has a built-in feature similar to Apple’s but not in the same styling.

Samsung is now preparing its own version of the Dynamic Island, and it seems this one has a bit more meat on its bones.

SamMobile on Twitter/X posted a video and two still images of what appears to be a Dynamic Island clone coming to Galaxy devices. It’s mentioned as potentially coming to the Galaxy S27 series (so, One UI 9.5) and being called “Moment Effects.” A portion of the software explicitly mentions integration with Google Sports, the leak claims, while it seems Samsung is using Live Notifications here, which already support a number of third-party apps.

	

	

The kicker from a UX perspective is that Samsung’s interpretation allows you to swipe between activities, similar to Apple, but the core premise is similar with the island showing around the selfie camera cutout.

When this feature might surface does remain unclear, but a One UI 9.5 debut would make plenty of sense. That update is in beta now and due to launch on the Galaxy S27 series early next year.

What do you think of Samsung’s alleged Dynamic Island clone? Personally, I’m on board as long as it proves useful, and it seems to be on the right track compared to most other copycats.

title: Google Health update fixes my biggest Fitbit Air complaint with ‘in-progress’ workout card
snippet: Google’s Fitbit Air is one of my favorite products of 2026 and my preferred workout companion, but not being able to see a workout while you’re in the middle of it has been a huge complaint of mine, and the latest Google Health update is fixing that. more…
fullText:
Google’s Fitbit Air is one of my favorite products of 2026 and my preferred workout companion, but not being able to see a workout while you’re in the middle of it has been a huge complaint of mine, and the latest Google Health update is fixing that.

Quite literally at the start of this week, I was on a walk through my neighborhood and though to myself, “it’s still pretty annoying that I can’t see my workout progress in the Google Health app.” It’s been a complaint of mine for a while, as various treadmill sessions and more have left me wondering what my heart rate is looking like, how many steps I’ve taken, etc, and it’s only a problem when using the Fitbit Air, seeing as the Pixel Watch (or Fitbit Edge) I’d wear otherwise will show that data front and center. 

Google Health 5.13 is fixing that.

In the changelog for Google Health 5.13, Google details a new “exercise in-progress” card on the main “Today” screen. This will show what exercise is being tracked and also let you end the workout early.

	

Google says:

If you use your Pixel Watch, Fitbit Air, or Fitbit Edge to automatically track your exercises, you’ll now see an exercise-in-progress card on your mobile app’s Today screen. This card lets you know that your device is tracking your exercise and gives you the opportunity to end the tracking and get your summary whenever you want.

We don’t know exactly what this card looks like just yet, but it sounds like it fits the need perfectly. 

Google Health 5.13 is now rolling out on Android and iOS.

title: Alleged Pixel 11 Pro prototype had HiLight and a temperature sensor
snippet: Google might have had a chance to keep the temperature sensor around, it seems, as a supposed prototype shows off a device that offered both the last-gen temperature sensor and the new HiLight LED in one. more…
fullText:
Google might have had a chance to keep the temperature sensor around, it seems, as a supposed prototype shows off a device that offered both the last-gen temperature sensor and the new HiLight LED in one.

	

Images posted to Telegram (via NotebookCheck) show an apparent prototype of the Pixel 11 Pro XL. The device is seen with the markings that are common to other known Pixel prototypes, with the key difference compared to the final model being the fact that the camera bar has both a temperature sensor and HiLight.

We can tell this is HiLight due to the diffused rear LED, and we know this isn’t a Pixel 10 Pro XL because the camera bar has full-width glass instead of a metal portion.

Google pulled the plug on the temperature sensor in Pixel 11 Pro after the prior three generations offered the feature. While the sensor was never particularly beloved, Google did see backlash from the lack of functionality in HiLight at launch. Having both features may have resulted in a different sentiment around the updated hardware.

title: Motorola accidentally releases ‘Moto Tag 3’ tracker early with new colors
snippet: Despite the fact that Moto Tag 2 has only been on the market for a few months at this point, Motorola is apparently getting Moto Tag 3 out in the not-too-distant future, and it’s already on sale (probably by mistake). more…
fullText:
Despite the fact that Moto Tag 2 has only been on the market for a few months at this point, Motorola is apparently getting Moto Tag 3 out in the not-too-distant future, and it’s already on sale (probably by mistake).

An Amazon UK listing went up this week for “Moto Tag 3,” a new version of Motorola’s Android Find Hub tracker. The listing shows the tracker in “Pantone Lucent White,” while a second image shared by Evan Blass shows the new model in a vibrant purple color.

There’s no indication of major changes in “Moto Tag 3,” with Motorola still claiming similar battery life, using a CR2032 battery, and supporting UWB in Android Find Hub.

The listing (thanks Matt!) explains:

	

Motorola moto tag 3 helps you locate everyday items with precision and reliability. Using Ultra Wideband and Bluetooth technology, it works with the Android Find Hub network to track belongings both nearby and at distance. With more than 500 days of battery life powered by a replaceable CR2032 battery, it is designed for long-term use. Built-in privacy protections, encrypted location data, and unwanted tracking alerts support secure tracking in a compact, IP68-rated design suitable for daily carry.

“Moto Tag 3” is on sale from Amazon UK, though it comes with a “1-4 month” shipping estimate. This is almost certainly a slip-up, especially given the timing.

This comes much earlier than expected. The original Moto Tag launched in 2024, with its sequel being announced in early 2026 before going on sale in the US less than six months ago in June 2026. Such an early move to “Moto Tag 3” is interesting, to say the least, so we’ll have to wait and see if there are any changes in tow beyond just the new colors. That said, these are really nice colors. It’s also possible this is just the same model with a slip-up in branding – the model number on the Amazon listing is unchanged.

We’ll have to wait and see what happens. Moto Tag 2 did debut at CES in January, and with Razr Flex also in the works, Motorola almost certainly would launch an updated tracker at the trade show if it truly does plan to do so soon.

This comes right as Moto Tag 2 has hit its lowest price ever at just $18.99 amid Black Friday sales.
